title: Give It a Reason
tagline: It's not our enemy right now. It's the only bridge on this lake.

intro.text: The lake gives it up slowly. First the shape of a shoulder, boulder-wide, stone-grey and crusted in moss and old barnacle scale. Then the rest — a hunched, standing bulk that shouldn't be able to hold that much stone above water and still move. A slab of rock rides across its back like something it's carried so long it forgot it could be an obstacle.

Its face is beaked, reptilian, cracks running through it that glow a sick yellow-green. It doesn't roar. It turns toward the sound they made, unhurried, the way something enormous turns when it has never once needed to be fast.

intro.speaker: Batra
intro.text: Well. We asked.

intro.speaker: Narrator
intro.text: A short, contemptuous flex of both arms sends corrosive water sheeting outward in a wide arc — less an attack than a shrug that happens to be lethal. Duke clears it clean. Batra doesn't bother.

intro.speaker: Batra
intro.text: ...Bigger bite than advertised.

intro.speaker: Duke
intro.text: That wasn't a person, Batra. Stop grading it like one.

intro.speaker: Batra
intro.text: Where's the fun in caution.

intro.speaker: Duke
intro.text: The fun in caution is still having that arm tomorrow.

outro.text: He doesn't listen. Not fully. It answers faster than the math should allow, and Duke closes the gap and hauls him sideways by the collar half a second before it would have connected clean. They go down together, rolling, close enough that the strike sprays them both.

outro.speaker: Duke
outro.text: You don't get unlimited second chances against something this size. You don't know where its ceiling is. You're not testing a person — you're gambling blind.

outro.speaker: Batra
outro.text: ...A Singh isn't supposed to flinch. Nobody mentioned the exam had giant rock lizards in it.

intro.text: That's when Duke sees it — the corrosion mark on Batra's forearm still lit faint green, and across the clearing, in perfect time with it, a matching brightness blooming through the cracks on Molvarr's hide. Like a second heartbeat answering the first.

intro.speaker: Duke
intro.text: ...Look.
Batra follows his eyes. Watches his own glow dim half a shade the exact instant Molvarr's brightens to match it. Too precise to be coincidence.

intro.speaker: Batra
intro.text: ...It's taking that. Right off me.

intro.speaker: Duke
intro.text: Every mark it leaves on us, it's cashing in later. I don't know how. But every time it lights up like that, we just made it stronger.

intro.speaker: Batra
intro.text: ...That is an extremely inconvenient rule.

outro.speaker: Narrator
outro.text: The fight changes shape from here — Batra pulling his hits inward instead of outward, refusing every lingering corrosive exchange even when it costs him tempo he's used to having, taking only the fast clean strikes from now on.

outro.speaker: Narrator
outro.text: Minutes in, they land everything they have in one coordinated push. It should mean something. It staggers, sinks half its bulk back beneath the surface like it's shrugging the damage off into the lake itself — and when it rises again the wounds are closing, water flowing back into the cracks.

outro.speaker: Batra
outro.text: ...Oh, come on.

outro.speaker: Duke
outro.text: It heals faster than we can out-damage it. We're not winning this on force.
He looks past it — past the thrashing bulk, past the water — to the flag on the island, still exactly as far away as it was an hour ago.

outro.speaker: Duke
outro.text: So we stop trying to win it. It's not our enemy right now. It's the only bridge on this lake.

outro.speaker: Batra
outro.text: ...Now you're speaking my language.

intro.text: It reads the shift in them and answers with something bigger — both arms drawing back, water gathering and compressing between its claws into something dense enough to bend light. It drives the strike at Batra specifically, the one who's hurt it most.

intro.speaker: Batra
intro.text: Arm's dead. Nothing there.

For a stretch it's Duke alone against something that outweighs him a dozen times over, at a range he's never had to answer for. Tao's voice, unbidden: you're exposed the moment your opponent steps outside your preferred range.

intro.speaker: Narrator
intro.text: So instead of forcing his way back into contact range, he starts reading it the way Lyra reads distance — feints, pressure released early, water thrown out ahead of himself instead of only through his fists. It's clumsy. It isn't his style. It keeps him alive.

intro.speaker: Batra
intro.text: ...Didn't know you could fight like that.

intro.speaker: Duke
intro.text: Neither did I, twenty seconds ago.

Then something changes. The glow in its cracked hide stops flickering and holds — brightens steadily, like a furnace catching. The stone slab across its back settles differently, like armour locking into place rather than dead weight being carried.

intro.speaker: Batra
intro.text: It was holding back.

intro.speaker: Duke
intro.text: It's not anymore.

outro.speaker: Batra
outro.text: The lake's trying to finish the job on its own.

outro.speaker: Duke
outro.text: Then we stop handing it more.

Batra reads the exact moment it commits to a full-body lunge — the kind that doesn't leave room to change its mind. He plants, draws everything he still has, and drives his ultimate not into the creature at all, but straight down into the water in front of it, point-blank.

outro.speaker: Narrator
outro.text: The corrosive lake doesn't splash. It flashes — a wall of superheated steam and displaced water exploding outward exactly as the lunge arrives, its own momentum carrying it through empty vapour where two people used to be standing.

Duke is already moving. Fist of Flowing Ruin was never about matching force — it was about redirecting it. He catches Batra by the collar and rides the surge, both of them carried on the wave rather than swimming through it, the last stretch closing in seconds neither could have covered on their own legs.

outro.speaker: Narrator
outro.text: They don't land so much as crash. Behind them the creature recovers slowly, thrashing once, twice, searching a stretch of water that no longer has anything worth finding in it.

outro.speaker: Batra
outro.text: We didn't beat that thing.

outro.speaker: Duke
outro.text: We weren't supposed to.

outro.speaker: Batra
outro.text: ...First time something's made me feel small.

outro.speaker: Duke
outro.text: Get used to it. We're apparently doing a lot of that now.

outro.speaker: Narrator
outro.text: Behind them, Molvarr gives up the search — sinking back beneath the surface, settling into whatever stillness it had before two candidates gave it a reason not to have any. They get up slowly, turn away from each other, and head toward separate parts of the course. The rest of Phase 2 is not a team sport.
